Cc: Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@brightlayer.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 10:15:00 -0400
Subject: Reserved capacity ask + sensitivity to GPU pricing

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. BrightLayer is excited by the latency profile and the autoscaling behavior for our inference pipelines. Before we move to legal, procurement asked for clarity on two items:

1) If we commit to a 24-month reserved pool for Aurora (as discussed), can the commit tenor include a GDP/market indexation clause for GPU spot price swings?
2) We need an option to scale down reserved units by up to 20% mid-term without immediate penalty if market GPU prices spike > 30% over baseline.

Attached is a strawman we drafted for optics (BL_Reserved_Term_Proposal_v2.pdf). Can you share what’s required on Redwood’s side for approval and whether finance would accept a conditional discount or tiered pass-through?

Best,
Sienna
Procurement Lead, BrightLayer

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sienna Park <sienna.park@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 13:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask + sensitivity to GPU pricing

Sienna —

Appreciate the clear asks and the draft. High level: we can offer a 24-month reserved capacity commitment with two mechanisms to mitigate GPU market shocks:

- Indexed adjustment trigger: if cloud GPU market index > 30% vs baseline for 30 consecutive days, we can open a reprice window to evaluate a temporary surcharge or a credit-based protection.
- Mid-term flex: one-time scale-down up to 20% without penalty if the trigger fires; scaling back up would be at then-prevailing prices with a short re-onboarding buffer.

We need to run these mechanics by finance and legal — Karthik and Ben are looped for the pricing and approval path. Can you confirm whether BrightLayer prefers credits, a temporary surcharge, or a blended discount if a trigger happens? That will help us size the protection.

I’ve attached our baseline GPU scenarios (gpu-pricing-scenarios.xlsx) and a redlineable proposal to start.

—Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 09:31:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity ask + sensitivity to GPU pricing

Team —

Quick take from GTM/finance perspective: we can support two levers but need a clearly defined SLA/trigger and a maximum exposure cap. Suggested approach:

1) Trigger definition: market index > 30% for 21 of 30 rolling days (gives noise tolerance).
2) Protection instrument: blended credit pool equal to X% of monthly commit spend, consumed only when trigger active. Credits are preferable to surcharges because they simplify revenue recognition and preserve customer experience.
3) Mid-term scale-down: allow one permitted scale-down (up to 20%) with a 90-day notice post-trigger; any subsequent scale actions would be considered a contract amendment.
4) Maximum exposure: cap Redwood’s downside at a 15% month-over-month equivalent subsidy across a 6-month window; beyond that we escalate to execs.

Ben — can you validate the accounting and whether a credit-based instrument passes our revenue rules? Also, we should price the initial 24-month commit assuming a 10% discount on public list for the baseline SKU mix and model mix assumptions Marissa included.

-Karthik
VP, Sales Operations

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 12:18:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity ask + sensitivity to GPU pricing

Karthik —

Finance comments: credits are workable but we need the following constraints to keep revenue accounting simple and limit P&L volatility:

- Credits must be capped at an aggregate dollar ceiling per deal (suggest: 6 months of committed spend as an upper bound).
- Credits consumed only while the trigger condition is met; leftover credits expire at contract end.
- Any mid-term scale-down needs a defined repricing band for returning capacity (e.g., re-adds priced at +5% vs remaining committed rate for 12 months).
- If the GPU market spike persists beyond 6 months, escalate to leadership for a one-off true-up.

I’ll draft the accounting language and a sample cap table for the credit instrument.

-Ben
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks — BrightLayer prefers a credit-first approach (credits consumed during the trigger window), and would like the cap to be communicated up front. Two clarifications from our side:

- The trigger window: can we shorten to 14 of 21 rolling days? Cloud vendors we benchmarked use a tighter window.
- Can the one-time mid-term scale-down be executed with 60 days notice instead of 90? Our Q4 budget exposure is tight and we’d prefer a faster reaction window.

Marcus will share procurement’s suggested cap number later today for modeling.

Sienna

Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask + sensitivity to GPU pricing

Sienna —

We can accept the tightened trigger (14 of 21 rolling days) and shorten the notice to 60 days for the one-time scale-down, with two caveats:

1) Credit cap: we propose a conservative default cap of 4 months committed spend for this deal size (we’ll populate the exact $ figure once Marcus sends the SKU mix). This keeps our maximum exposure bounded while giving BrightLayer meaningful protection.
2) Re-onboarding price: any re-add within 12 months is priced at the then-prevailing committed rate +/- a small market adjustment (we propose +3% if market index remains > baseline).

Next steps: Marcus to share SKU mix and target cap. I’ll have Ben circulate a redline with the credit cap language and Karthik will prepare an exec summary for approval if we exceed the 4-month default.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
